title: Hexagon-Net: Heterogeneous Cross-View Aligned Graph Attention Networks for Implied Volatility Surface Prediction

problem.claim: Implied Volatility Surface prediction must support options hedging, portfolio management, and risk control while handling imbalanced data distributions and forecasting uncertainty.

gap.claim: Existing approaches do not adequately handle changing moneyness and maturities, uneven regional information, or complex cross-perspective interconnections in the IVS.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes Hexagon-Net, an end-to-end heterogeneous cross-view aligned graph attention network for IVS prediction.
Hexagon-Net aligns historical IVS data, learns distinctive IVS patterns, propagates predictive information, and forecasts future IVS movements jointly.
The paper reports experiments including ablations, sensitivity analyses, and alternative configurations to investigate the model's performance.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present Hexagon-Net as a novel heterogeneous cross-view aligned graph attention network.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on stock index options datasets report that Hexagon-Net significantly and consistently outperforms previous approaches in IVS modeling and deep learning.
Ablation studies, sensitivity analyses, and alternative configurations are reported as investigations of the reasons for the model's superior performance.

narrative_sequence.summary: IVS prediction is important for financial risk-related applications and faces imbalance and uncertainty challenges.
Deep learning has made progress, but several structural and informational problems remain unresolved.
Hexagon-Net addresses the stated problems through heterogeneous cross-view alignment and graph attention.
Experiments report consistent performance improvements and analyses of the reported advantage.

source_observation.claim: IVS regions are unevenly informed because of liquidity constraints and should not be modeled uniformly.

interpretation.claim: Prediction architectures may need region-specific or heterogeneous treatment when information availability varies across the input space.

application.claim: For related structured forecasting problems, model heterogeneity in data informativeness rather than applying uniform processing everywhere.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that heterogeneous treatment is beneficial outside IVS prediction or under different liquidity conditions.

source_observation.claim: Moneyness and maturities change over time, making spatio-temporal alignment necessary before forecasting.

interpretation.claim: Inputs whose coordinates or meanings shift over time require explicit alignment before downstream prediction.

application.claim: Use explicit temporal and spatial alignment in forecasting pipelines when the observed structure changes across time.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify which alignment procedure is used or whether it generalizes to other changing coordinate systems.

unknowns: Dataset identities, sizes, time periods, and preprocessing are unspecified.
Evaluation metrics, numerical results, baselines, and statistical significance are unspecified.
The alignment, graph construction, attention mechanism, and forecasting horizon are unspecified.
